name: duplimend_optimized_v1
description: The exact DupliMend configuration used for every result reported in the paper.
derived_from: median (numeric) / mode (categorical) across the 4 group-level Bayesian-optimization winners

provenance.note: Seed 42 was used ONLY for the hyperparameter search. The reported results are ten independent evaluation runs with seeds 1-10; see seeds.json.

derived_values._hidden_dims_rule: hidden_dims = [2 * layer_size, layer_size] for n_hidden_layers = 2; the encoder is [256, 128] -> latent 64 and the decoder mirrors it.

env_var_mapping._comment: config/config.py reads every parameter from these environment variables at import time. config/paper_config.py emits exactly this mapping.

discovery_params._source: Stated in the paper: models are discovered with the Inductive Miner at a noise threshold of 0.2, imported via PM4Py.
discovery_params._repo_mismatch: The noise threshold is NOT APPLIED anywhere in the shipped code. evaluation_core.py line 37 computes `inductive_miner_noise_threshold` (from NOISE_THRESHOLD, else config.py's 0.0, else 0.2) but the variable is never read again: all discovery call sites (evaluation_core.py lines 576, 701, 748) call `inductive_miner.apply(log)` with no noise parameter, as does generate_ground_truth.py line 179. Setting NOISE_THRESHOLD therefore has no effect. To honour the published 0.2, the threshold must be passed to the miner at those call sites.
discovery_params._observed_effect: Measured on I-PALIA: passing noise_threshold=0.2 explicitly yields the identical model (10 places, 11 transitions) and identical metrics as the default, so on this log the setting is immaterial. Not yet measured on the real-life logs.
metrics_reported: F-score (harmonic mean of Precision and Fitness)
discovery_params.checkpoint: Results are reported at the final 100% checkpoint.

differs_from_repo_defaults._comment: IMPORTANT for reproduction: the committed defaults in config/config.py are development defaults, NOT the paper configuration. Running main.py without applying this config will not reproduce the reported numbers. Each entry is [repo_default, paper_value].

warmup_note: warmup_proportion = 0.20 means the warm-up phase consumes the first 20% of each log's events. config/config.py instead takes an ABSOLUTE event count via WARMUP_EVENTS, so scripts/run_paper_experiments.py computes WARMUP_EVENTS = round(0.20 * n_events) per log. Note the committed default (warmup_global_events = 4000, annotated in config/config.py as '~50% of I-PALIA') is a development default and does not correspond to the 20% proportion used in the paper; it must be overridden per log.
